judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseResult wrapper ({success, data}) and GoogleCalendarService writes that wrapper object directly into credential.key instead of the parsed .data, replacing the flat credential JSON. Every Google Calendar token refresh (which fires ~hourly once access tokens expire) rewrites the stored credential as {"success":true,"data":{...}}; on the next load the top-level access_token/refresh_token are gone, so every Google Calendar operation for every user fails until the row is manually unwrapped in the DB or the user re-authenticates. This corrupts credentials in the default configuration (no credential-sharing env vars set), i.e. every deployment of this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, ... }`), not the parsed `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential `key` is set to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then written to Prisma (`data: { key }`). This will persist the wrapper object into `credential.key` (e.g. `{success:true,data:{...}}`) instead of the expected flat credential payload, effectively corrupting the stored credential for subsequent reads/uses. This happens in the non-credential-sharing path as well because the function still uses `schema.safeParse(...)` and returns that wrapper.
